Siri AI already debuted on most Apple platforms back in June, but Apple TV and HomePod were left out. However, the latest leak suggests Siri AI will finally arrive with tvOS 27.

Apple heavily promoted 'One Siri' at WWDC, but tvOS and HomePod were overlooked

When Apple finally officially unveiled its AI version of Siri this summer, it emphasised that this was a complete overhaul from scratch, designed to work consistently across all your devices.

David Clark, Apple's senior director of watchOS software engineering, explained to TechRadar:

'One Siri' is something many users have wanted for years. The most frustrating thing is when you ask Siri to do something, it tells you to ask again on another device.

However, this declaration of a unified Siri experience made no mention whatsoever of the Apple TV 4K or HomePod. These two products virtually disappeared at WWDC, with only a handful of features mentioned.

I'd long assumed Siri AI would land on Apple TV and HomePod this autumn, but Apple hasn't announced that yet, possibly because it will become an exclusive feature for as-yet-unannounced hardware.

Now, new evidence within tvOS 27 appears to confirm this—at least for Apple TV.

tvOS 27 lists an internal codename for Siri AI in its Device Hub app list

When running Device Hub via Xcode in macOS 27, the tvOS 27 app list gains a new entry: Siri.

The Siri entry contains the string 'com.apple.campo'. Previous reports have indicated that 'campos' is Apple's internal codename for Siri AI.

Comparing the app lists of the tvOS 26 and tvOS 27 simulator modes confirms that the 'Siri' entry is absent from tvOS 26. It has only been newly added in tvOS 27.

This new entry, combined with the word 'campo', strongly suggests Siri AI will make its debut this autumn alongside tvOS 27. There may even be a standalone Siri app on Apple TV—though this isn't yet confirmed, because the 'apps' list includes system features in addition to user-facing apps.

When attempting to open 'Campo.app' within Device Hub, an error message pops up:

There are no further details for now. So we don't know, for instance, whether the new Siri AI features will support existing hardware.

However, at this point, it's safe to say that Siri AI will be the main selling point Apple uses to market its next-generation Apple TV 4K hardware.
